# OpenCode for Blender `@neuralnomads/opencode-blender` lets OpenCode read and change the scene open in Blender 5.3 or later. It is a `native` integration: the **OpenCode Link** add-on runs an authenticated host inside Blender, and the plugin sends it typed, revision-checked batches, fixed inspection and render programs, and (asking each time) Python code. No Blender documentation is bundled: the plugin asks the running Blender what it exposes and links the official documentation of its version. > **Status: preview (draft 0.2, `spec: 0`, RPC contract 1).** Not published to npm yet. ## Installation ### Any OpenCode client 1. Add the plugin to the `plugins` list of your **global** OpenCode configuration (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`). Native integrations are installed in the global configuration only. ```jsonc { "plugins": ["@neuralnomads/opencode-blender@^0.4"] } ``` With options (all optional, see [Options](#options)): ```jsonc { "plugins": [{ "package": "@neuralnomads/opencode-blender@^0.4", "options": { "hostInspectionDir": "/path/to/extensions/user_default" } }] } ``` 2. Install the add-on: ask OpenCode to run `blender_install_host` (it asks for permission), or install `host/blender/opencode_link-.zip` from the package with Blender's **Preferences ▸ Get Extensions ▸ Install from Disk**. The add-on is installed on the computer that runs OpenCode, in the user extensions folder of the newest Blender 5.3 or later started there. 3. In Blender, enable **OpenCode Link** (Preferences ▸ Add-ons). While it is enabled, the session is offered to OpenCode, at every start included; disabling it withdraws the offer. 4. In OpenCode, use any Blender tool: with one Blender open and attached to no other conversation, the first call attaches it to this conversation. With several, `blender_hosts` lists them and `blender_hosts` with `attach` attaches one (it asks for permission). ### In CodeNomad The **Plugins** section lists OpenCode for Blender as an integration: its version, whether the add-on is installed and up to date, and whether the conversation is attached; its menu installs or updates the add-on after a confirmation and detaches the conversation. **Plugins ▸ Add** also accepts the package name. ## Chat in Blender (prototype) With OpenCode running and OpenCode Link enabled, open a **Python Console** (`Shift–F4`) and choose **Console → Languages → Opencode**. It connects on its own, even for an unsaved scene, and keeps the current conversation when you open another file in the same folder. Use the conversation menu in the header, or `/list` then `/open `, to switch. **New conversation** (`/new`) stays empty until you send a message. `/stop` interrupts or clears queued messages; `/status` and `/help` are always available. The console uses OpenCode’s executable; Node.js 22+ (`NEURALNOMADS_BLENDER_NODE` or `PATH`) is only a fallback. The add-on preferences can target a named OpenCode service. The Console wraps lines and keeps its own Up-arrow history. An unfinished line appears when the stream finishes or the next newline arrives. **Copy as Script** copies this area's scrollback as plain text, not executable Python. Earlier messages stay in OpenCode when you reconnect; they are not replayed into Blender. `/allow` approves a single pending OpenCode permission once; `/reject` declines it. Use OpenCode to handle questions or multiple pending approvals. CodeNomad can stay attached separately. Blender cannot repaint or accept console input while a main-thread Python operation or bake is running. Output queues and appears once the main thread is free; `/stop` does not preempt Python already running in Blender. ## How it works - **Discovery and consent.** While OpenCode Link is enabled, the add-on listens on `127.0.0.1` on a random port with a random 256-bit token kept in memory, and offers the session to every OpenCode service registered for your user (or to one: the add-on setting _OpenCode service_). Offers last 15 seconds and are renewed every 5 seconds. - **Attachment.** A conversation acts on the Blender attached to it. The only offered Blender, compatible and attached to no conversation, attaches itself at the conversation's first Blender call, without asking; otherwise `blender_hosts` with `attach` asks the `blender_attach` permission. Opening another file in Blender replaces the offer: the conversation attaches again the same way. - **Which Blender.** `blender_hosts` and `blender_context` name the Blender this conversation acts on (`attached_to`: offer and label). Other conversations attaching or detaching other Blenders, or Blenders appearing, never make this conversation's ownership unverifiable; a permission prompt is refused only when this conversation's own Blender changed meanwhile. - **Across an OpenCode restart.** The plugin keeps each conversation's attachment in its storage (the Blender's offer key only as a SHA-256 digest, with the label; never a token, port or script handle). When the same Blender offers itself again after a restart, the conversation is attached back without asking, once its ownership is verified at its Location; never inside a read. A kept attachment lasts while its Blender is offered and two minutes after it stops; detaching removes it at once. A Blender restarted itself is a new offer: the conversation attaches again as above. - **Upgrading without restarting OpenCode.** A daemon that loads a newer version of the plugin without restarting can keep the older one in memory. Each version keeps its own list of offered Blenders, named after the add-on versions it accepts, so a Blender is always judged by the version that lists it; it offers itself again within 5 seconds. - **The working method.** When a conversation attaches a Blender, a short method joins it (an instructions entry, about 250 tokens): read the Blender version first, inspect the exact element before coding it, read an error's hint and inspect again instead of guessing, turn each requirement of the task into a check, run every check on the saved file (`blender_verify` with `saved: true`: the file is what is delivered), and report each requirement with its measured value, saying what failed or was not checked. - **Session binding.** Clients read `bindingRead({ sessionID })` at the session's current OpenCode Location: `attached` identifies its live offer and safe label, `none` confirms a verified session without a binding, and `unknown` keeps the state unverified. `status_changed {}` invalidates the read; `detachHost({ sessionID })` detaches. See the [draft 0.2 RPC contract](../../../spec/rpc-contract.md). ## Tools | Tool | What it does | | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `blender_hosts` | The offered Blenders (label, document, Blender version, whether this conversation or another one is attached to each) and the add-on's install state; `attach` attaches one (asks permission), `detach` releases this conversation's. | | `blender_install_host` | Installs or updates OpenCode Link in the newest Blender 5.3 or later (asks permission). | | `blender_context` | A compact read of the scene: revision, scene settings, collections, markers, a page of objects with their transforms; `ref` gives one object in detail (world bounds, pose bones); `include: ["parts"]` lists a mesh's loose parts (world box, material, dominant vertex group), `region` keeps those in a world box. | | `blender_apply` | Up to 50 typed operations as one undo step, checked whole before anything changes; a failure part-way restores every changed field. The deleted objects leave the document when the batch succeeds, with the data only they used. - **`duplicate`** copies a hierarchy into the originals' collections, keeps each child's parenting, points constraints at the copies and shares materials and actions; `linked` also shares the data. A `name` or `suffix` another object holds is refused before anything runs. - **`set_material`** creates a Principled material when no material has that name, or sets the values of an existing one; a value Blender would clamp fails the batch, which is restored. - **`scene_settings`** never lets Blender push the other end of the frame range: one end crossing the other is refused. `fps` 23.976 sets fps 24 and its base. - **`shift_keys`** moves keys with both handles (or deletes them) in the action slot the object uses (Blender 5 layered actions); a key landing on one that does not move is refused. ## Options | Option | Environment variable | Default | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | `hostInspectionDir` | `NEURALNOMADS_BLENDER_HOST_INSPECTION_DIR` | The user extensions folder of the newest Blender 5.3 or later | | `requestTimeoutMs` | `NEURALNOMADS_BLENDER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | 120000 (1 s to 10 min); a verification render waits 10 min | Add-on settings (Preferences ▸ Add-ons ▸ OpenCode Link): _OpenCode service_ (offer to one service only), _OpenCode configuration folder_ (only for a service started with `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`), and **Reset OpenCode Link** after a failed restoration. ## Permissions | Permission | Asked when | | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `blender_attach` | `blender_hosts` attaches a Blender (never for the automatic attachment) | | `blender_install_host` | `blender_install_host` installs or updates the add-on | | `blender_execute_code` | every `blender_execute_code` run | | `blender_import` | `blender_import` imports an asset or a file (never for a search) | ## Code execution `blender_execute_code` runs Python in Blender with your rights: it can read and write files, start processes and reach the network. The add-on lists it while it is enabled, and **every run asks the `blender_execute_code` permission** ("ask" unless you allow it in OpenCode's permission settings); a refused run executes nothing. A run that changes the scene is one undo step; a failing one is undone. Blender keeps linked data outside its undo (a linked library, the brush a sculpt or paint mode links): it is named in `restoration.kept_linked`, unused and not saved. When an undo cannot be proven, OpenCode Link is **quarantined**: reads, `blender_verify`, `blender_inspect` and `read_only` code still run, changes wait; `blender_context` shows `quarantine.may_have_changed`, and once you checked it, `blender_context` with `release_quarantine` (that read's revision) lifts it, as does Reset in the add-on's panel. A long script can be a file (`path`): it is read as written, with no escaping through a JSON or JavaScript string, and its tracebacks name the file. See [`SECURITY.md`](../../../SECURITY.md). When the open document differs from its file, the results of `blender_context`, `blender_apply`, `blender_execute_code` and `blender_verify` carry `unsaved`: the file's name (`never_saved` for a new document) and the OpenCode steps since its last save or load (changes made by hand are not listed); saving a copy leaves it, a run that saves the open file and changes nothing after clears it, and a run that opens a file pushes no step into it. A run that fails on Blender's API carries a `hint` read from that Blender before the run is undone: for an unknown attribute, the closest names and the type's properties; for an operator's arguments, its real signature (with the element type of its collections) and the closest names; for an invalid enumeration value, the closest items; for a missing key, the collection's keys (a node's sockets included); for an unknown node type, the closest types the tree creates, with their sockets; for a failed poll, Blender's reason, the context the code had, the operators of its group whose poll passes, and the context members (with their path) or editor area that make it pass, found by trying `poll()` only. While a run executes, OpenCode Link prepares two calls Blender 5.3 closes on from a script, as Blender's interactive path prepares them, and says so in `warnings`: a mask stroke (`sculpt.brush_stroke` with the Mask brush or `brush_toggle='MASK'`) on a multiresolution object gets its mask layer first, and in a Blender without interface a sculpt-mode operator gets a first undo step when none was pushed yet. If the attached Blender crashes, the call running then stops waiting within two seconds and says so with the crash report Blender wrote (`.crash.txt` in its temporary folder; only the report named after its own document counts, since every Blender of a user writes there); on Windows its process stays open behind Blender's crash window. A Blender closed without a report (closed, or ended by another program), one whose offer stopped while its process runs, and a call that outlasts its wait while Blender still runs it (the add-on's `status` answers off Blender's main thread, with the request running and for how long) are said as such; after its Blender crashed or closed, a conversation never attaches another Blender by itself. ## Blender limits - Blender 5.3 or later; edits run in Object mode only. - Two conversations may attach the same Blender: each batch is checked against the document's revision, and the attach that makes it shared says so (`shared`). - Blender 5.3 closes when a script sets `use_disk_cache` on the rigid body world's point cache of a saved file (a Blender defect, outside OpenCode Link). - The code-change fingerprint that keeps the revision current does not read mesh vertices, modifier and node values or settings below one nested level. A `read_only` run is judged by its content instead (poses, mesh vertices, shape key values, constraint influences, material node values): one that puts everything back is no change. ## Earlier installation A `blender` plugin file in the global configuration, or a listener answering the earlier bridge's ping on port 9876, is reported as `legacy_install` in `status`. Remove it: both would compete with this plugin. ## Development ```sh npm run build --workspace @neuralnomads/opencode-blender # dist/ (checks the host artifacts) npm run build:host --workspace @neuralnomads/opencode-blender # the add-on payload and the marker's digest python integrations/blender/host/ops_json.py # host/ops.json and the table above node --test integrations/blender/test/*.test.ts # BLENDER_TEST_BIN= for the host tests ``` What 0.4.0 keeps, replaces and retires from 0.2.0, and how to reintroduce a retired part: [`METHODS.md`](METHODS.md). ## Licence MIT for the plugin; GPL-3.0-or-later for the add-on, the Blender Lab tool code it contains and the programs run in Blender (see [`NOTICE.md`](NOTICE.md)).

The `license` field of `package.json` is `MIT AND GPL-3.0-or-later`, as the repository's packaging rules require of a package that embeds a GPL-3.0-or-later application part: the plugin's licence and the add-on's. The programs run in Blender's Python like the add-on and share its licence. No Blender documentation is bundled: `blender_inspect` reads the running Blender and links the official documentation of its version.
